title: Body-mass–lung-volume coupling does not establish incremental dyspnea prediction across two NHANES samples
abstract: Motivated by prior SCAPIS interaction evidence, a frozen BMI-by-height-normalized-log-FVC product was tested beyond flexible standard spirometry and covariates. In2571 independent-sample NHANES2009–10 adults, weighted Brier error improved by0.00001874(0.0109%),but target-only and source-refit design-bootstrap95%intervals crossed zero and source grouped crossvalidation worsened. This negative representation test does not establish incremental utility or refute obesity-related respiratory physiology.
